Lemma
[Dirichlet's Approximation Theorem]

1. ch4:4.21For every $\alpha \in \mathbb R$ and positive integer $N$, there are integers $n,m$ with $1\le n\le N$ such that $|n\alpha -m|<1/N$.

Proof

\sketch Set $f(x)=x-\lfloor x\rfloor $. The $N+1$ values $f(i\alpha )$ for $0\le i\le N$ lie in $[0,1)$, so two, say with $0\le i<j\le N$, lie in the same one of the $N$ intervals $[k/N,(k+1)/N)$. Hence $|f(j\alpha )-f(i\alpha )|<1/N$. Taking $n=j-i$ and $m=\lfloor j\alpha \rfloor -\lfloor i\alpha \rfloor $ proves the claim.
